elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 7.7 reads in full: "Customer shall pay no liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." The 15%-per-week formula in the original p0032 is deleted entirely, leaving no retained instalment, formula or contingent liquidated payment mechanic; the prohibition is unconditional and Agreement-wide. Rationale confirms no other Customer-payable liquidated amount exists (9.4 accrued Fees only; Section 27 termination without penalty; Section 3 credits run to Customer).

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind survives ("Customer shall pay no liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement"), so there is no liquidated amount that could be anything other than an early-termination fee. The preferred outcome subsumes this fallback element.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee is imposed anywhere in the redlined text (Section 9.4 termination without cause obliges only accrued Fees), so there is no amount requiring a three-month cap. The cap is referenced only in the margin comment as a negotiating concession, which is not needed because no fee exists in the operative text.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the operative sentence eliminates all Customer-payable liquidated amounts, so a fortiori none competes with an (absent) early-termination fee.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the sole target element is delivered by an unconditional, operative sentence rather than a promise in the comment, and the offending 15%/week formula is fully removed rather than merely narrowed.

Minimality holds: the change is confined to Section 7.7, replacing the deleted LD mechanic with one concise sentence. No survival tail, no damages carve-outs, no procedure, no at-own-expense or boilerplate extras, and no words outside the LD mechanic were touched (late-payment interest, suspension and other payment remedies elsewhere are left intact).

Intent preserved: nothing in the cited material cross-references the deleted 15% formula, no defined term is left undefined ("Fees" remains used only in untouched clauses), and Sections 3, 9.4 and 27 remain internally consistent with a no-liquidated-damages result.

Deterministic gates (operation applies, minimality, element coverage) are consistent with the substance on inspection; the replacement text is genuinely unconditional and leaves no contingent payment formula.

No action required by the drafter; the fallback cap language sensibly stays in the comment as a concession rather than being drafted into the operative text, which would otherwise reintroduce a Customer-payable liquidated amount unnecessarily.
